scholarships.title: University of Auckland International Student Excellence Scholarship

existing.description: The University of Auckland International Student Excellence Scholarship is a tuition fee credit of up to 25% of one year of tuition fees for new international master's students at Waipapa Taumata Rau. There is no separate application: eligible students who hold a conditional or unconditional programme offer by 20 October 2026 are invited by the Scholarships Office on 21 October 2026 to complete a supplementary application form, which must be submitted by 4 November 2026. Applicants must be international students with an Admissions GPE of at least 7.0 and must complete at least two consecutive semesters of study or repay the value. The award is made on the recommendation of a selection committee and granted by the Vice-Chancellor.
eligibility: Have received a conditional or unconditional offer of admission to an eligible masters programme at the University
Have an Admissions GPE of at least 7.0
Not have already commenced study at the University
Not have undertaken any tertiary level study in New Zealand, excluding a student exchange programme
Not be enrolling as a distance education student, including University of Auckland Online
Graduate School of Management applicants only eligible for the Master of Applied Finance, Master of Business Analytics or Master of Professional Accounting
existing.eligibility_summary: New international students who hold a conditional or unconditional offer of admission to an eligible master's programme at Waipapa Taumata Rau by 20 October 2026, with an Admissions GPE of at least 7.0. Excludes students who have already commenced study at the University or have undertaken tertiary study in New Zealand (other than exchange), distance/online enrolments, and most Graduate School of Management programmes.
benefits: Tuition fee credit of up to 25% of one year of tuition fees
Offered twice a year (Semester One and Semester Two intakes)
coverage: Tuition fees credit of up to 25% of the recipient's tuition fees for the first two semesters of their masters degree
requirements: Hold an offer or conditional offer of admission by 20 October 2026
Accept the scholarship offer by the date stated in the awarding notification, otherwise the offer is forfeited
Enrol full-time in the applicable masters programme
Complete at least two consecutive semesters of study at the University
documents: Supplementary scholarship application form submitted through the online application portal
Personal statement (assessed as a selection criterion)
existing.english_requirement: Not stated as a separate scholarship requirement on the official scholarship page; international admission English language requirements apply through the offer of admission.
application_method: No separate scholarship application at the time of programme application
Invited applicants complete a supplementary application form in the online application portal
existing.selection_notes: Granted by the Vice-Chancellor after receiving a recommendation from a selection committee comprising the Director International (or nominee) and two faculty Associate Deans (International). Selection criteria are academic merit as assessed by the Admissions GPE and the quality of the applicant's personal statement; the applicant's country of origin and alignment of the intended programme with the University's strategic objectives may also inform selection.
existing.best_fit: High-achieving new international master's applicants with an Admissions GPE of 7.0 or above who already hold or will hold a conditional offer for Semester One or Quarter Two 2027.
existing.application_period: Semester One / Quarter Two 2027 intake; invitations issued 21 October 2026, supplementary forms due 4 November 2026
existing.deadline_display: Invitations will be issued on 21 October 2026 to eligible students to complete a supplementary application form. Supplementary application forms must be submitted online by 4 November 2026 to be considered.
existing.program_type: Tuition fee credit for new international master's students

scholarships.title: University of Auckland Doctoral Scholarship
scholarships.degree: PhD, DMedSc, DClinPsy, DocFA, EdD, DHSc

existing.description: The University of Auckland Doctoral Scholarship is a competitive scheme run in four awarding rounds each year for high-achieving candidates applying for admission to an approved doctoral programme at Waipapa Taumata Rau. In 2026 it provides a tax-free stipend of $35,468 per annum with an annual CPI adjustment for up to 42 months full-time equivalent, compulsory tuition fees and the Student Services Fee for the same period, and the single student health insurance charge where applicable. No separate scholarship application is needed — the candidate confirms in the doctoral programme application that they wish to be considered, and must not enrol before the outcome is advised. The 2027 dates table gives the next apply-by date as 1 November 2026.
eligibility: Be applying for admission to an approved doctoral programme (PhD, DMedSc, DClinPsy, DocFA, EdD or DHSc) at Waipapa Taumata Rau
Indicate in the doctoral programme application that you wish to be considered for the scholarship
Not enrol in the doctoral programme before the University has considered you for the scholarship and advised you of the outcome
Be prepared to take up the scholarship by one of the enrolment dates prescribed in the letter of award
existing.eligibility_summary: High-achieving candidates applying for admission to an approved doctoral programme at Waipapa Taumata Rau. There is no separate scholarship application: the candidate indicates in the doctoral programme application that they wish to be considered for the scholarship, and must not enrol in the programme before scholarship consideration has concluded and the outcome has been advised.
benefits: Tax-free stipend of $35,468 per annum in 2026, adjusted annually by CPI from 1 January each year
Full compulsory tuition fees and Student Services Fee for up to 42 months FTE
Single student health insurance charge for international students
International students can request a funding confirmation letter through Student Services Online for visa purposes
coverage: Tax-free stipend of $35,468 per annum in 2026 with annual CPI adjustment, for up to 42 months FTE
Compulsory tuition fees and Student Services Fee for prescribed study in the doctoral programme, up to 42 months FTE
Single student Health Insurance compulsory charge for international students, where applicable
requirements: Indicate the wish to be considered for a University of Auckland Doctoral Scholarship in the doctoral programme application
Do not enrol in the doctoral programme before scholarship consideration has concluded and the outcome has been advised
Take up the scholarship by one of the dates prescribed in the letter of award, otherwise the offer is forfeited
Enrol by the prescribed date, which differs for domestic candidates and international candidates
documents: Doctoral programme application form, including the confirmation that the applicant wishes to be considered for the scholarship
Records of prior study and research proposal assessed as part of doctoral admission (not separately published for the scholarship)
existing.english_requirement: Not stated on the official doctoral scholarship pages; English language proficiency is assessed through admission to the doctoral programme.
application_method: Apply for a doctoral programme at the University of Auckland and tick the scholarship consideration option in the application form
There is no separate scholarship application and no online scholarship application form
existing.selection_notes: Any student offered a place in a doctoral programme is considered for the scholarship. Scholarship selection committees consider the University's equity, diversity and inclusion objectives and the applicant's gender and ethnicity, plus any voluntarily disclosed disability, Rainbow community or refugee background information, when making their recommendations. Guaranteed scholarships exist for Māori and Pacific applicants with a New Zealand university qualifying programme GPA of 7.0 or above who are offered a place in a doctoral programme.
existing.best_fit: Doctoral candidates who are applying for admission to an approved doctoral programme at Waipapa Taumata Rau and can meet the scholarship's enrolment deadlines, including international candidates needing tuition, stipend and health insurance support.
existing.application_period: Four awarding rounds each year. For 2027 entry the rounds are 1 November 2026, 1 February 2027, 1 May 2027 and 1 August 2027 (apply-by dates).
existing.deadline_display: The scheme runs four awarding rounds each year. In the 2027 dates table the next applicable round is "Apply by 1 November 2026"; the record page also lists the closing dates as 1 February, 1 May, 1 August and 1 November.
